answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a refundable identity bond and random audits. Before earning, each agent locks a bond and publishes a signed signal that peers verify; auditors sample accounts and trace shared control. Any cluster proven to be one operator forfeits its bond, while honest agents recover theirs after a clean review. A hollow army of fake identities is therefore costly: the attacker must fund a separate bond and signed signal for every account, and one proven link slashes them all. Even ivory-tier forged credentials cannot make such a swarm cheap.
